The largest sample size in the library and the strongest HEALING signal at this entry tier. 66% positive responses, 76% reporting noticeable-or-better improvement, with 59% settling within 10 minutes. AutoGluon predicts 6.859 — notably below observed, indicating real-world performance exceeds model expectation (contradictory signal). H-OS-L2.name: Rainfall

H-OS-L2.sphere_plain: Reliable for quieting overstimulation, though some find the music pleasant but not deeply moving.

H-OS-L3.name: Glacier
H-OS-L3.sphere: n=47, mean=7.04 (std=1.68, meaningful confidence). 78% report improvement with two-thirds positive. Qualitative data shows strong sleep-context use (8 of 23 'trying to sleep'), suggesting the deepest OS variant finds a sleep-adjacent user base. AutoGluon's overstimulation prediction of 6.859 is ~0.2 below observed. Notably, this protocol is the most analytically distinct in cross-protocol clustering (mean_sim=0.677) — consistent with its dual sleep/overstimulation use profile.
H-OS-L3.sphere_plain: Good for winding down, especially before sleep. Feels steady and quiet, almost meditative.

H-AX-L1.name: Meadow
H-AX-L1.sphere: n=67, mean=7.22 (std=1.93, strong confidence). Distribution shows moderate right-skew without bimodality — 63% of responses in the 7-10 range. Qualitative feedback indicates moderate-to-significant improvement with modal settle time of 10 minutes; 87% of respondents rate rhythm as balanced or calming. YouTube visibility is minimal at 7 views. AutoGluon's anxiety-zone prediction of 7.838 aligns within noise, supporting this protocol as a well-calibrated design. Panel largely converged on framing this as a core HEALING anchor.
H-AX-L1.sphere_plain: Many people find real relief from anxiety with this protocol — it works quickly and the steady rhythm feels grounding. It's one of the more reliably helpful tracks in the library.

H-AX-L2.name: Cottage
H-AX-L2.sphere: n=48, mean=6.94 (std=1.62, meaningful confidence). Qualitative data shows a noticeable-improvement mode with 5-minute settle dominance and neutral music opinion in 25% of respondents. YouTube reach at 6 views remains negligible. AutoGluon predicts 7.838 for the anxiety zone — a ~0.9 delta above observed, suggesting either under-sampling or a slightly weak groove fit relative to L1. The tighter std versus L1 indicates more consistent but slightly damped response.
H-AX-L2.sphere_plain: A gentler version that takes a bit longer to land but still helps most listeners feel more settled. The music is comfortable rather than deeply affecting.

H-AX-L3.name: Valley
H-AX-L3.sphere: n=36, mean=7.08 (std=1.89, meaningful confidence). The wider std reflects a slower-onset profile — qualitative data shows 20% of listeners settling only near session end, consistent with the longer arc. 75% report improvement. AutoGluon's anxiety-zone prediction of 7.838 is ~0.75 above observed. YouTube views at 4 are essentially absent. The panel converges on viewing L3 as the deep-entry anxiety option with reliable but delayed effect.
H-AX-L3.sphere_plain: Works best for people who need a longer, slower journey into calm. Some find it takes the whole session to feel the shift, but the relief tends to last.

H-CR-L1.name: Anchor

Qualitative data is more positive than the mean suggests — 33% report significant improvement and 67% improved noticeably-plus — indicating the score distribution includes a subgroup still in acute states. AutoGluon's crisis-zone prediction of 7.955 sits ~1.6 above observed, suggesting a gap the model attributes to insufficient stabilization time. Panel converged: hold-phase extension warranted.
H-CR-L1.sphere_plain: For people in acute distress, this offers a starting point of relief — many feel meaningfully better. It may not hold the effect long enough for everyone.

H-CR-L2.name: Harbor
H-CR-L2.sphere: n=33, mean=6.52 (std=1.70, meaningful confidence). H-CR-L2.sphere_plain: Slightly more grounding than L1 for crisis moments, though some people don't connect with the music itself.

H-CR-L3.name: Horizon

sphere_commentary.overview:
Across 1000 outcome responses the three series show differentiated profiles that align with design intent, with widespread converging signal on HEALING's consistency and THRIVING's cognitive peaks.
• HEALING (n=574, mean=6.98, std=1.77) leads in reliability — the lowest variance in the dataset, consistent with its regulation mandate
• THRIVING (n=245, mean=6.96, std=1.72) matches HEALING's mean despite smaller n, with T-FC-L3 recording the highest single-protocol score (7.63)
• TRANSFORMING (n=181, mean=6.59, std=1.87) trails modestly with widest spread, structurally expected for ascending-arc targets
• YouTube retention data is uniformly NULL across the dataset — all reach signals are weak and should not be over-interpreted until views exceed 50
sphere_commentary.cross_series:
Series-level efficacy patterns track functional design intent, with observable tension between observed means and AutoGluon predicted scores in TRANSFORMING zones.
• HEALING protocols cluster tightly between 6.35–7.22, with H-CR-* structurally lower but H-OS-* and H-AX-* the strongest
• THRIVING HOLD protocols show tight peaking at L3 — T-FC-L3 (7.63) and T-CF-L3 (7.28) both reward deeper arc structure
• TRANSFORMING carries the largest predictive gap — AutoGluon estimates 7.5–8.2 across X-MC/MD/ME zones while observed means sit 1.0–2.5 lower, suggesting either model overfit or unmet protocol potential
• DESCENT designs (HEALING, X-MC) outperform ASCENT designs (X-MD, X-ME) in observed means — a pattern warranting investigation
sphere_commentary.anomalies:
Several protocols diverge from series norms in ways that warrant flagging, though most reflect structural rather than failure patterns.
• X-MC-L3 (n=10) — mean 5.70 with std 2.45 is the largest negative deviation in the library; high variance and low n suggest genuine population mismatch rather than signal
• H-CR-L1 (n=43) — mean 6.35 sits 1.5 below the lowest AutoGluon crisis prediction (7.955 for H-CR-L2), structurally expected for crisis listeners arriving in extreme states
• X-ME-L1/L2 — AutoGluon's top two predictions (8.23) unchallenged by YouTube views (8 each), suggesting either suppressed potential or undiscovered efficacy
• T-FC-L1 vs T-FC-L3 — L1 mean 6.46 vs L3 mean 7.63 represents the largest within-protocol-family gradient in the dataset, suggesting ascending hold duration materially drives focus outcomes
sphere_commentary.development_signals:
[CONVERGENT SIGNAL] H-OS-L1 (n=95) records the strongest HEALING signal at mean 7.15 yet remains largely undiscovered — suggest increasing reach via channel amplification to translate efficacy into population use
• H-CR-L1/L2/L3 — all underperform the AutoGluon crisis prediction of 7.955 by ~1.5 points; consider extending hold phase length to deepen stabilization before protocol termination
• X-MC-L3 (n=10) — bimodal distribution and low mean warrant either redesign as a longer L4 variant or repurposing as a niche subgroup protocol rather than core library
• T-FC-L3 (n=35) — highest outcome score in THRIVING but only 15 YouTube views; consider launching an L2 cross-volume variant to validate that the ascending-hold benefit transfers across grooves
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] X-ME-L1 (n=39) — AutoGluon predicts 8.23 vs observed 6.74, the largest absolute gap in the dataset; investigate whether current entry conditions underserve this protocol's design intent
sphere_commentary.embedding_analysis:
Cross-run drift is pervasive across the library, suggesting either evolving response patterns or interpretive recalibration as data accumulates since early-2026.
• CROSS-RUN DRIFT: 29 of 31 protocols show notable drift below the 0.85 similarity threshold, most extreme in X-MD-L3 (0.507), H-SL-L1 (0.530), T-FC-L3 (0.532), and X-ME-L2 (0.532) — this pattern suggests the data itself is evolving faster than Sphere's prior framing, not analytical instability
• CROSS-PROTOCOL SEMANTIC CLUSTERS: T-FC-L1/L2 pair most tightly (0.878) and H-SL-L1/L2/L3 cluster as expected by category; H-OS-L3 is most analytically distinct (mean_sim=0.677), consistent with its highest engagement in qualitative listener-type breakdowns
• Confidence note: drift values are based on 3 run snapshots since 2026-04-02 — sufficient for trend detection but insufficient to distinguish sampling noise from genuine signal evolution; re-evaluate at n>=50 per protocol

by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L1: Many people find real relief from anxiety with this protocol — it works quickly and the steady rhythm feels grounding. It's one of the more reliably helpful tracks in the library.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L2: A gentler version that takes a bit longer to land but still helps most listeners feel more settled. The music is comfortable rather than deeply affecting.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L3: Works best for people who need a longer, slower journey into calm. Some find it takes the whole session to feel the shift, but the relief tends to last.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L1: For people in acute distress, this offers a starting point of relief — many feel meaningfully better. It may not hold the effect long enough for everyone.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L2: Slightly more grounding than L1 for crisis moments, though some people don't connect with the music itself.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L3: Fastest to settle for some but more polarizing overall — works well for those who connect, feels too gentle for others.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L1: One of the strongest overstimulation tracks — most people feel noticeably more settled within about ten minutes. The music is generally well-liked.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L2: Reliable for quieting overstimulation, though some find the music pleasant but not deeply moving.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L3: Good for winding down, especially before sleep. Feels steady and quiet, almost meditative.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L1: One of the better sleep tracks — most people settle quickly and enjoy the music. Often reported as genuinely useful for falling asleep.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L2: Helpful for many but more mixed — some find the rhythm too active for deep sleep, especially if they're very sensitive to busy patterns.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L3: Calms many people quickly, but the rhythm can feel slightly busy for the deepest rest. Most still notice improvement.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L1: A gentle creative-flow support — subtle rather than dramatic. Works best for people already halfway into a flow state.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L2: Slightly more activating than L1, with more listeners reporting real creative gains. The music is well-liked.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L3: Shows the strongest creative-flow signal of the three, possibly because the longer arc has time to unfold. More testing would help confirm.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L1: Helps some people focus but the rhythm can feel a bit busy for sensitive listeners. Better for those who like a more active groove.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L2: A noticeably better focus experience than L1 — most people feel clearer and more on-task after about ten minutes.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L3: The strongest focus track in the library — most listeners report feeling meaningfully sharper. Some gravitate to the music especially.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L1: A steady, gentle maintenance track. Doesn't push or pull — just supports where you are. Takes a while to settle but feels grounded.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L2: More variable than other maintenance tracks — helps some people a lot, leaves others unmoved. The rhythm may be too active for the middle length.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L3: Some people settle well, others don't connect at all. Still developing — wait for more feedback before drawing conclusions.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L1: Helps with mental clarity for most, though a small number find it doesn't suit them. The music is generally well-loved.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L2: Works for people who find the right entry — fast settling for some, slower for others. Naturally discovered more than most mind-clarity tracks.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L3: Currently doesn't land well for most people — a small subset responds very positively but many feel it doesn't suit them. Likely needs redesign.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L1: Helps some listeners with motivation but results are quite mixed. The quick onset may not give enough time for the effect to deepen.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L2: The longest settling time in the motivation set — works for patient listeners but may feel too gradual for those wanting quick drive.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L3: Surprisingly the strongest in the motivation family — the longer arc may be what motivation needs. Variable results suggest it really depends on the person.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L1: A potentially powerful track that may not be reaching the right people yet. When it works, listeners describe meaningful energy shifts.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L2: Similar to L1 in feel — slow onset, strong music reception. Works best for people willing to give it time.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L3: Currently the weakest in this family — some people feel energized but many report no effect. Unclear whether the design or the audience is the issue.
